newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Canada given a month to act on US magazine dispute.
newsitem.headline: Canada given a month to act on US magazine dispute.

text.p: The World Trade Organisation (WTO) formally ruled on Wednesday that Canadian taxes on local editions of foreign magazines discriminated against foreign products, trade officials said.

The WTO's Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) approved findings of an appeals board earlier this month which rejected Canadian arguments against a ruling by a dispute panel in February that the taxes run against WTO open trading rules.

The consensus approval of the panel and appeals board findings by the DSB, on which all 131 members of the WTO have a voice, also means Canada has until August 29 to propose a plan on how it will implement the ruling.
Trade officials said Canada's ambassador John Weekes told the DSB that the measures had been primarily aimed at protecting the country's national culture from foreign domination.

U.S. delegate Scott Anderson, also repeating arguments presented during the case, responded that WTO members could not be allowed to use the "defence of culture" argument to discriminate against foreign goods.
Washington brought the case against Ottawa following the imposition in December 1995 of an 80 percent tax on advertising in U.S. periodicals that publish editions in Canada.
The tax hit the Canadian edition of Sports Illustrated, owned by Time Warner Inc, which was subsequently closed down.
Under WTO rules, Canada would have 15 months to implement the panel recommendations after August 29, trade officials said.
If it declines, the DSB could authorise the United States to take sanctions against Canada to the value of trade deemed to have been lost.
